evidence.output: PROBE-C status=200 log=[POST /p 200 0ms in=1025 out=2 rid=...]; tests=3 failures=0
evidence.intent_output: FR-APP-028 asks in= to count the bytes read through bodyStream on the same BodyState counting path as the other readers; no AC fixes the value after an overrun.

findings.drop_reason: in=1025 (limit+1) counts the one probe byte LimitedInputStream takes from the wire to detect the overrun. That is the shared BodyState counting path FR-APP-028 asks for, and the JSON reader logs the same value. No AC is violated.
findings.title: Access log in= after an overrun is limit+1, not the 1024 bytes handed to the handler
findings.description: After an overrun through bodyStream(1024), the access log shows in=1025 because the probe byte is counted.
findings.suggested_fix: None needed. If wanted, document in FR-APP-019 that in= includes the overrun probe byte.

evidence.command: ./gradlew -PtinyHttpdFromMaven=true :NaruServe-api:test --tests 'com.snoworca.naruserve.ScratchReviewRawBodyTest' (probe escaped413OfTheCallHasTheStandardBody: rawBodyLimit(1024), Content-Length 1025, handler lets bodyStream()'s HttpException escape)
evidence.intent_output: FR-HTTP-031 AC-4: the bodyStream call throws HttpException 413 before any byte is read.

findings.drop_reason: Status 413 is correct. The empty body comes from the harness StubJsonCodec, which cannot encode the error map; the same happens for every standard error under that codec. Not a defect.
findings.title: 413 from a declared length over the limit reaches the client
findings.description: Checked that an unhandled HttpException 413 thrown by bodyStream() becomes a 413 response.

evidence.command: ./gradlew -PtinyHttpdFromMaven=true :NaruServe-api:test --tests 'com.snoworca.naruserve.ScratchReviewRawBodyTest' (probe concurrentCallsGetTheSameStream: 16 concurrent req.bodyStream() calls from 8 threads in one handler)
evidence.output: all 16 futures returned the same object; test passed
evidence.intent_output: FR-HTTP-030 AC-6/AC-7: a repeated call with an equal limit before consumption returns the same object.

findings.drop_reason: No race found. rawLock serializes creation, the lock order is rawLock -> BodyState -> inputLock, and closeBody never takes rawLock, so there is no cycle.
findings.title: Concurrent bodyStream() calls
findings.description: Checked the thread safety of rawStream's repeat rule under contention.

evidence.output: 205: throw new ParseError(400, "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length"); 228: conflicting Content-Length; 249/255: invalid Content-Length
evidence.intent_output: FR-HTTP-031: the declared Content-Length decides the early 413 and caps the stream.

findings.drop_reason: contentLength() trusts the first Content-Length header, and with both TE and CL it would cap a chunked body at CL. TinyHttpd rejects TE+CL, conflicting CL and invalid CL with 400 before dispatch, and the JSON reader has the same pre-existing behavior.
findings.title: Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding could truncate the raw stream
findings.description: Possible request-smuggling-style truncation if an adapter passed both headers through.

evidence.output: val chained: RestApp = app.rawBodyLimit(512L shl 20).jsonLimit(1024L) also compiles when the result is the platform type RestApp!
evidence.intent_output: IR-APP-009 AC-6: chained call without a platform type.

findings.drop_reason: The Kotlin test alone cannot tell RestApp from RestApp!, but its comment says so, and RawBodyLimitTest.IR_APP_009_AC6_rawBodyLimitCarriesNoNullnessEscape pins the @NullMarked scope by reflection. The pair covers the AC.
findings.title: Kotlin AC-6 test does not by itself tell a platform type apart
findings.description: A test-quality concern; it is covered by the Java companion test.

clean_code.description: bodyStream(long) repeats the 1..MAX_LIMIT range check and message that DefaultRestApp.byteLimit (DefaultRestApp.java:300-305) already has; the two can drift apart.

clean_code.principle: DRY / one default in one place
clean_code.description: The rawBodyLimit default 1048576 is set in three places: DefaultRestApp.java:116, Dispatcher.java:63 and DefaultRequest.java:72. All three borrow JsonBodyReader.DEFAULT_LIMIT, so the raw limit is coupled to a constant named for the JSON reader.

rawBodyLimit reaches Dispatcher and DefaultRequest through post-construction setters (as proxyTrust does), while jsonLimit and formLimit go through the constructors. Forgetting a setter at a new construction site silently falls back to the default.
InputExchange (RequestBodyStreamTest) and CountingExchange (RequestBodyStreamLimitsTest.java:305-345) are near-identical HttpExchange delegates to RecordingExchange. They could share one test helper.
RawBodyStream repeats the markSupported/mark/reset refusal that its LimitedInputStream source already has.
